start.meta.description.message: No technical background? No problem. Run through five steps in 20 minutes and let AI finish your first real task today.

start.hero.title.message: 20 minutes to your first real AI task

start.hero.lead.message: This page doesn't explain theory, it gets you doing. Finish the five steps and you'll have a result you can actually use, plus a method you can reuse. No programming needed.

start.steps.lead.message: Do them in order. None of them is long, and you can stop to try things out at any point.

start.faq.lead.message: We get asked these a lot, so here are the answers up front.

start.cta.title.message: Finished all five steps? Next stop: the learning roadmap

start.cta.text.message: The roadmap tells you what to learn in each of the next three stages and what counts as done, so you don't get lost in an endless stream of tutorials.

start.step1.title.message: Pick one main AI assistant — just one

start.step1.p1.message: The most common beginner trap is opening five AI accounts, using each one a little and knowing none of them well. Pick one as your main tool and stick with it for two full weeks.

start.step1.li1.message: Want the most general-purpose option with the richest ecosystem → pick ChatGPT

start.step1.li2.message: Often read long documents, write long pieces, care about a natural tone → pick Claude

start.step1.li3.message: Already live in Gmail / Google Docs → pick Gemini

start.step1.p2.message: All three have free tiers, which are plenty while you're starting out. For a detailed comparison, see the {link}.

start.step2.p1.message: Before you paste your first piece of text, remember this rule:

start.step2.p1.strong.message: if you wouldn't want a colleague to see it, don't paste it into AI.

start.step2.li1.message: ID numbers, bank accounts, medical records, passwords: never paste them

start.step2.li2.message: Customer lists, unpublished quotes, internal documents: check your company policy first

start.step2.li3.message: If you must paste something, replace names with placeholders such as "Person A" or "Company A"

start.step3.title.message: Use one formula to get your first good answer

start.step3.p1.message: Stop typing just "write me an email". Use this four-part formula and the quality of your answers changes immediately:

start.step3.formula.role.message: : You are a marketing planner with ten years of experience.

start.step3.formula.task.message: : Write an outreach email proposing a collaboration.

start.step3.formula.context.message: : The recipient is the marketing manager of a coffee chain; we are a local roaster hoping to discuss a co-branded product. Our strengths are small-batch customisation and a local story.

start.step3.formula.format.message: : Under 300 words, conversational but professional, ending with two concrete proposals.

start.step3.p2.message: Swap those four lines for your own situation, paste it into AI and see the difference. More techniques in the {link}.

start.step4.title.message: Pick one annoying weekly task and hand it to AI once

start.step4.p1.message: You don't learn AI by finishing tutorials, you learn it by finishing the first real task. Pick one of these now, then keep reading:

start.step4.li1.message: Turn a long meeting transcript into 5 conclusions and 3 action items

start.step4.li2.message: Take an email you're struggling with and ask AI for three versions in different tones

start.step4.li3.message: Take an English article you can't get through and ask AI for the key points as bullets

start.step4.li4.message: Take a pile of messy ideas and ask AI to organise them into a slide outline

start.step5.p1.message: AI says wrong things in a very confident tone — that's called hallucination. Anything that affects a decision has to be checked:

start.step5.li1.message: Numbers, dates, legal clauses, prices → always verify from another source

start.step5.li2.message: Books, papers or URLs it cites → open them and confirm they exist

start.step5.li3.message: Ask it back: "What is this claim based on? Could it be wrong?"

start.step5.p2.message: For the reasoning and the full process, see {link}.

start.faq1.q.message: I'm not good with computers at all — can I still learn this?

start.faq1.a.message: Yes. Everything here assumes you have no technical background and uses plain language. If you can type in a browser, you can start.

start.faq2.q.message: Do I have to pay for a subscription?

start.faq2.a.message: No. Free tiers are plenty while you're starting out. Once you're using AI every day and clearly hitting the limits, then it's worth paying.

start.faq3.a.message: A more realistic way to put it: people who use AI well will pull ahead. Rather than worrying about it, become one of them — that's exactly why this site exists.

start.faq4.q.message: Do I need to learn to code?

start.faq4.a.message: No. The main path here needs no programming background at all. If you later want to build small tools, just read the vibe coding chapter.

start.faq5.q.message: How much time does this take each day?

start.faq5.a.message: Fifteen minutes a day, and in two weeks you'll notice the difference. The key is using AI on real work rather than setting aside extra time to "study AI".

roadmap.principle1.text.message: Don't learn AI for its own sake. Pick something you already have to do this week and try it with AI — that's what makes the learning stick.

roadmap.principle2.title.message: Change one variable at a time

roadmap.principle2.text.message: Switch tools, models or phrasing one at a time. Otherwise you'll never know which change made the result better.

roadmap.principle3.text.message: When you get a great answer, save that prompt to your notes right away. Three months later those notes beat any tutorial.

roadmap.principle4.text.message: AI handles drafts and speed; you handle facts and responsibility. Your name is on it, so verifying is your job too.
